analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, workflow BASE/HEAD, patches and documentation against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. In .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml:112-138,194-198 (HEAD), listing aggregation moves from jq arguments to files in the existing private temporary directory; HTTPS, token handling, pagination and response-size limits remain unchanged. This removes an argument-size availability failure without introducing observed command injection or credential exposure.
HEAD:239-242 removes recent completions and the attempt's last completion as rescue blockers. Cancellation can now interrupt other running shards or follow recent progress when an old queued job has received no runner. This is explicitly documented in changelog.d/darkbloom-watchdog-listing-size.md:4-5 and docs/developer/build.md:442-448. Legitimate resource-limit waits may therefore be cancelled sooner; no supplied evidence establishes an attacker-controlled prerequisite or a violated security guarantee sufficient for a finding. Existing marker checks, rescue limits, attempt recheck and cancellation/rerun handling remain visible at workflow HEAD:244-297.
No provider authorization, attestation, encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing implementation or privileged local control is changed. The GitHub rescue mechanism is distinct from the provider rollback watchdog in T-043. Integration should verify the route job's fallback contract and the safety of cancelling/re-running partially completed build/release jobs: HEAD:164-179 assumes the rerun selects appropriate fallback runners, but their configuration and affected callers are not supplied. These are unverified cross-file contracts, not evidence of unsafe fallback or duplicate publication.
